programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Boban is Fuigheag taiceil do dhaolag-bhreac a tha na suain ach, aig a' cheann thall, tha iad ag ionnsachadh nach e peata a th’ innte Boban and Fuigheag are helpful to a sleeping ladybird today, but at the end of the day they learn that it’s not a pet.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ bèicearachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Beth agus Isaac cuide ri Linda agus iad a’ fuine cèic le cnò-chòco agus smeuragan. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad dèanamh cinnteach gu bheil a h-uile cail tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha smeuragan a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson a’ cheic a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe! Linda Macleod and friends cook a number of tasty dishes. She is joined by Beth and Isaac to bake a delicious coconut and blackberry cake. However, before they start, they must be sure they have all the ingredients. If not, they make a list and go shopping. Linda and her friends also find out more about how blackberries are grown, and then it's back into the kitchen to bake the cake before sitting down at the table to taste it.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Air latha brèagha earraich, tha bèibidhean aig Blor! Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh ag ionnsachadh mun t-saothair a tha an lùib a bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh bèibidhean a tha a’ fàs. On a beautiful springtime day, it looks like Bop's had little babies! Abney and Teal find out just how much trouble growing babies can be.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean ag ionnsachadh dè tha gabhail àite fon talamh – air leth inntinneach! Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are learning what happens underground - really interesting!

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Grandad's gnomes go missing and Stan's mystery deepens when he finds a tiny human handprint! The gnomes can't really have come to life, can they?! Tha frìdean an t-Seanair a' dol a dhìth,'s tha rùn-dìomhair Dan a' dol am meud nuair a lorgas e làrach-làimhe beag bìodach bho dhaonna. 'N eil rian gun tàinig na fridean beò, a bheil?!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Patsi NicCoinnich a’ leughadh An Jazz Chù. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Maire Voigt agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Patsi Mackenzie reads An Jazz Chù, written by Maire Voigt and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc: Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Hannah a’ tadhal orra? The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge, but who will emerge victorious as Hannah joins them?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha sàr-fhiosaiche a’ bhaile, Madam Dhòmhnaill, a’ toirt rabhadh do Phòl gun coiseach fo àradh, no thig droch fhortan na rathad. Tha e a’ coiseach fo àradh co-dhiù is goirid às dèidh seo tha dreag a’ dèanamh air a' bhaile. Tha e an urra ri Pòl agus a charaid Raibeart Ròbot a glacadh mus sgrios i am baile. Dave is warned by local fortune teller Madam Donald that walking under a ladder will bring bad luck. He walks under one anyway, and soon a meteor is heading for Grimsby. It is up to Dave and his friend Robert Robot to catch it before everyone is squished.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Anna a’ trèanadh a bhith na draoidh agus ’s e Pòl an neach-taic aice. Chan eil iad ro mhath air rudan a chur à sealladh, gus a bheil Ceitidh Sombaidh a’ toirt leabhar gheasan draoidheil dhaibh. Anna is training to be a magician with Dave as her helpful assistant. Their disappearing trick is not up to much though, that is until Zombie Katie bestows a magic spell book upon them.

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Bekah! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha i ag innse dhuinn mu Bhoireannaich ann am Fànas agus mun obair chudromach a tha iad air a dhèanamh. Bidh i cuideachd a’ toirt sùil air teothachd san fhànais. Blast off into space with Astronaut Bekah! In this amazing space voyage, she tells us about the valuable work of women in space. She also takes a look at temperature in the cosmos.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Hilda, Flòraidh is Daibhidh a’ feuchainn ri bràisd’ nan eun a chosnadh, tha iad a’ tighinn tarsainn air Bhictòria Van Gèil. Tha a beatha ùr, ciùin a’ fàgail Dhaibhidh glè amharasach mu dèidhinn. De tha i ris? When Hilda, Flòraidh and Daibhidh are focusing on birding badges, they run into Victòria Van Gèil. She is very calm these days, and this new change arouses Daibhidh’s suspicion about her. What is she up to?

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Ball-coise air BBC ALBA/Football on BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Football action from the League One play-offs, first leg.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Às dèidh toiseach tòiseachaidh dùbhlanach, lean Somhairle agus Innes orra a’ rothaireachd air a Bhadger Divide, far an tàinig iad tarsainn air duilgheadasan meacanaigeach; uisge trom; geàrr-rathaidean; tionndadh ceàrr agus bagannan caillte! Thàinig an rothaiche agus an neach-gleidhidh chlàran, Kerry Nic a’Phì, còmhla riutha airson earrann. After a tough start, Somhairle and Innes continue riding the Badger Divide, where they encounter mechanical issues, torrential rain, shortcuts, wrong turns and lost baggage! They’re joined for a section by record-holder, cyclist Kerry MacPhee.

programme.title: Chernobyl – Utopia na Smàl/Chernobyl – Utopia in Flames
programme.desc: Fhad ’s a tha a’ choimhearsnachd eadar-nàiseanta ag èigheachd airson soilleireachadh mu thubaist Chernobyl, tha na stiùirichean Sobhieteach ann am Mosgo a’ cur an coire air an luchd-obrach fhèin. Anns an eadar-ama, tha Nickolai Steinberg a’ dèanamh a h-uile càil a ’s urrainn dha airson neo-chionntas a chuid co-obraichean a dhearbhadh. While the international community demands clarification about the Chernobyl accident, the Soviet leadership in Moscow makes the operating personnel the scapegoats of the disaster. Meanwhile, Nikolai Steinberg does everything he can to prove the innocence of his former colleagues. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by close friend Finlay Macleod from Scalpay for the final fishing trip of the season. With summer fading, the environment looks very different as the purple heather really comes to the fore. Tracked by the golden eagle, they sail north to the hamlet of Calbost to take advantage of the shelter offered by its bay on a less than optimal day. As the duo fish in the bay, they ponder the extremes of the sea - its matchless beauty and its mortal danger. Anns a’ phrògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha Fionnlagh MacLeòid à Sgalpaigh, còmhla ri Aonghas airson an turas iasgaich mu dheireadh den t-seusan. Leis an samhradh a’ tighinn gu crìoch, tha an àrainneachd a’ coimhead gu math eadar-dhealaichte, ‘s am fraoch purpaidh a’ tighinn am follais. Air an leantainn le iolaire-bhuidhe, seòlaidh iad gu tuath, gu Calbost gus beagan fasgadh fhaighinn sa bhàgh, air latha meadhanach grod. Fhad ’s a tha iad ag iasgach, tha iad a’ meòrachadh air an dà chuid cunnart agus bòidhchead na mara.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Bidh Iain MacFhionghain a' tòiseachadh streath ùr de Alleluia le measgachadh de laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean. Anns a’ chiad phrògram, bidh Iain a leughadh cosamhlachd agus cluinnear laoidhean freagarrach, feadhainn air an clàradh as ùr airson Alleluia. Am measg nan seinneadairean bidh Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ seinn An t-Seann Chladh Thall agus Dòmhnall-Iain MacIlleDhuinn a’ seinn Anns a’ Chrann. Bhon tasglann cluinnear Catrìona Watt a’ seinn Air Geugan Seilich. An t-seachdain-sa cluinnidh sinn leughaidhean agus smuaintean bhon t-Urr Daibhidh MacNeacail agus bho Kathleen Reddy agus bidh Iain fhèin cuideachd a’ leughadh earrann bho Chosamhlachdan. Iain MacKinnon reads a parable and introduces fitting hymns and psalms - some recorded especially for the programme. Eilidh Cormack performs An t-Seann Chladh Thall and Donald-Iain Brown sings Anns a’ Chrann. From the extensive Alleluia! archives, an opportunity to hear Catriona Watt singing Air Geugan Seilich. Rev David Nicolson and Kathleen Reddy each present their chosen reading from the Bible and related reflections. In Gaelic with English subtitles

However, she changes her mind when she learns that Rose's new boyfriend, a well-to-do Greek businessman, will be picking her and Richard up from their home in his limousine. programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: Simon Schama's epic history reaches the 18th century and the birth of modern Britain. Due to an economic explosion, the consumer society is born, agriculture becomes big business and London becomes the fastest growing city in Europe. However, many in Scotland are unhappy with the union of the Scottish and English parliaments. When Bonnie Prince Charlie and his Jacobite army advance on London, the country's new-found peace and prosperity are threatened.

programme.title: Berlusconi: Condemned to Win
programme.desc: Fabio Capello leads Milan to a new era of glory, while Berlusconi steps onto Italy’s political stage, ushering in a turbulent new chapter in the nation’s politics.

programme.title: Florence Nightingale: Nursing Pioneer
programme.desc: This film follows the life of an extraordinary woman who revolutionised modern nursing and whose legacy continues to benefit millions. Born into a rich English family, Florence Nightingale broke through social and gender barriers to pioneer a profession previously reserved for men. Dedicating her life to helping those in need, she was a trailblazer who led a group of nurses to care for wounded soldiers during the Crimean War and developed revolutionary views about hygiene and sanitation. Hailed as a heroine by Queen Victoria and the British people upon her return from the front, Florence went on to establish the Nightingale Training School for Nurses and reform healthcare at home and abroad. Florence Nightingale died in 1910 aged 90, leaving behind an inspirational legacy.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team explore the remarkable story of Jodrell Bank Observatory and its towering Lovell Telescope, which scientists have used to listen to the cosmos for almost 70 years.

programme.title: Dam Busters Declassified
programme.desc: Martin Shaw takes a fresh look at one of the most famous war stories of them all. The actor, himself a pilot, takes to the skies to retrace the route of the 1943 raid by 617 Squadron which used bouncing bombs to destroy German dams. He sheds new light on the story as he separates the fact from the myth behind this tale of courage and ingenuity. Using the 1955 movie The Dam Busters as a vehicle to deconstruct the raid, he tries to piece together a picture of perhaps the most daring attack in the history of aviation warfare. Along the way, Shaw hears from the last RAF veteran of the raid, as well as a German survivor of the tsunami which resulted from the Moehne dam's destruction.

programme.desc: This film follows the life of an extraordinary woman who revolutionised modern nursing and whose legacy continues to benefit millions. Born into a rich English family, Florence Nightingale broke through social and gender barriers to pioneer a profession previously reserved for men. Dedicating her life to helping those in need, she was a trailblazer who led a group of nurses to care for wounded soldiers during the Crimean War and developed revolutionary views about hygiene and sanitation. Hailed as a heroine by Queen Victoria and the British people upon her return from the front, Florence went on to establish the Nightingale Training School for Nurses and reform healthcare at home and abroad. Florence Nightingale died in 1910 aged 90, leaving behind an inspirational legacy.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team explore the remarkable story of Jodrell Bank Observatory and its towering Lovell Telescope, which scientists have used to listen to the cosmos for almost 70 years.

programme.title: Dam Busters Declassified
programme.desc: Martin Shaw takes a fresh look at one of the most famous war stories of them all. The actor, himself a pilot, takes to the skies to retrace the route of the 1943 raid by 617 Squadron which used bouncing bombs to destroy German dams. He sheds new light on the story as he separates the fact from the myth behind this tale of courage and ingenuity. Using the 1955 movie The Dam Busters as a vehicle to deconstruct the raid, he tries to piece together a picture of perhaps the most daring attack in the history of aviation warfare. Along the way, Shaw hears from the last RAF veteran of the raid, as well as a German survivor of the tsunami which resulted from the Moehne dam's destruction.

programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp presents a special show on a matter close to her heart – art! In Scotland’s capital city Edinburgh, she finds out about a group of famous local artists known as the Scottish colourists and speaks to the grandson of one of them. She also picks out some arty purchases from the show’s archives and counts down the most profitable items at auction. Along the way, Christina Trevanion visits the studio of an art restorer who brings works of art back to their former glory, and Charlie Ross is in mid Wales to meet an artist who sculpts countryside animals from clay.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team investigate the work of a scammer pretending to be from Amazon. He is trying to scam a man in the UK by saying that hackers have access to his online account, but it’s all a lie designed to get him to hand over money. The team’s access to the scammer is unprecedented, meaning they can see him running his criminal scam, live from his bedroom via his own webcam. And having access to the fraudster’s computer means that Nick and Harleen can learn almost everything about him – giving them the perfect opportunity to confront him.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Jan, Mick, Shirl and Dave – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring comedian and actor Charlie Brooks, Dr Amir Khan, presenter Sara Damergi and comedian Tim Vine as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp presents a special show on a matter close to her heart – art! In Scotland’s capital city Edinburgh, she finds out about a group of famous local artists known as the Scottish colourists and speaks to the grandson of one of them. programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team investigate the work of a scammer pretending to be from Amazon. He is trying to scam a man in the UK by saying that hackers have access to his online account, but it’s all a lie designed to get him to hand over money. The team’s access to the scammer is unprecedented, meaning they can see him running his criminal scam, live from his bedroom via his own webcam. And having access to the fraudster’s computer means that Nick and Harleen can learn almost everything about him – giving them the perfect opportunity to confront him.

programme.desc: The team hear from the devastated homeowners who claim the warehouses behind their back gardens were built without proper consultation. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp presents a special show on a matter close to her heart – art! In Scotland’s capital city Edinburgh, she finds out about a group of famous local artists known as the Scottish colourists and speaks to the grandson of one of them. She also picks out some arty purchases from the show’s archives and counts down the most profitable items at auction. Along the way, Christina Trevanion visits the studio of an art restorer who brings works of art back to their former glory, and Charlie Ross is in mid Wales to meet an artist who sculpts countryside animals from clay.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team investigate the work of a scammer pretending to be from Amazon. The team’s access to the scammer is unprecedented, meaning they can see him running his criminal scam, live from his bedroom via his own webcam. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Jan, Mick, Shirl and Dave – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Officers attending a call to a house where a woman has been punched in the face are confronted by a man with a large knife. There is a tense stand-off before they are able to cuff and arrest him. Stephen challenges a man arrested for a hate-motivated crime close to Belfast city centre. There are comical scenes as the Peelers try to herd cattle through the busy streets of west Belfast. Back in the city centre, Dave and Owen come across a group of drug users openly injecting cocaine in broad daylight, in a public square. As they arrive, they find one man still injecting. A tense stand-off ensues and police describe how they have to deal with the drug abuse and homeless crisis. Elsewhere, officers are called to reports of a street fight between two women. While trying to establish order amid the chaos, one woman wrestles with police, biting Anna and spitting blood into Tom and Adam’s eyes. She’s taken into custody wearing a spit and bite guard. Stephen looks on as the visibly distressed woman is processed through the police system. He is deeply affected by what he sees and hears – an unflinching view of the reality of frontline policing.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Officers attending a call to a house where a woman has been punched in the face are confronted by a man with a large knife. There is a tense stand-off before they are able to cuff and arrest him. Stephen challenges a man arrested for a hate-motivated crime close to Belfast city centre. There are comical scenes as the Peelers try to herd cattle through the busy streets of west Belfast. Back in the city centre, Dave and Owen come across a group of drug users openly injecting cocaine in broad daylight, in a public square. As they arrive, they find one man still injecting. A tense stand-off ensues and police describe how they have to deal with the drug abuse and homeless crisis. Elsewhere, officers are called to reports of a street fight between two women. While trying to establish order amid the chaos, one woman wrestles with police, biting Anna and spitting blood into Tom and Adam’s eyes. She’s taken into custody wearing a spit and bite guard. Stephen looks on as the visibly distressed woman is processed through the police system. He is deeply affected by what he sees and hears – an unflinching view of the reality of frontline policing.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team hear from the devastated homeowners who claim the warehouses behind their back gardens were built without proper consultation. programme.desc: Two properties with plans for both to be turned into serviced accommodation in London and Kent. Dion’s in Stoke, and rather than dancing on the ceiling. he’s bouncing on the floors!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp presents a special show on a matter close to her heart – art! In Scotland’s capital city Edinburgh, she finds out about a group of famous local artists known as the Scottish colourists and speaks to the grandson of one of them. She also picks out some arty purchases from the show’s archives and counts down the most profitable items at auction. Along the way, Christina Trevanion visits the studio of an art restorer who brings works of art back to their former glory, and Charlie Ross is in mid Wales to meet an artist who sculpts countryside animals from clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team investigate the work of a scammer pretending to be from Amazon. He is trying to scam a man in the UK by saying that hackers have access to his online account, but it’s all a lie designed to get him to hand over money. The team’s access to the scammer is unprecedented, meaning they can see him running his criminal scam, live from his bedroom via his own webcam. And having access to the fraudster’s computer means that Nick and Harleen can learn almost everything about him – giving them the perfect opportunity to confront him.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Choirmaster Gareth Malone is hoping that the New Forest property market hits all the right notes as he enlists the help of Sonali Shah to find him and his family a new home in the Hampshire countryside. With mum Sian along for assistance, Gareth has one big request: to find a property with enough space to fit a grand piano! A beautifully converted former schoolhouse may just provide the answer, but the endless possibilities and potential at a 1920s thatched cottage really strike a chord with the music maestro.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp presents a special show on a matter close to her heart – art! In Scotland’s capital city Edinburgh, she finds out about a group of famous local artists known as the Scottish colourists and speaks to the grandson of one of them. She also picks out some arty purchases from the show’s archives and counts down the most profitable items at auction. Along the way, Christina Trevanion visits the studio of an art restorer who brings works of art back to their former glory, and Charlie Ross is in mid Wales to meet an artist who sculpts countryside animals from clay.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team investigate the work of a scammer pretending to be from Amazon. He is trying to scam a man in the UK by saying that hackers have access to his online account, but it’s all a lie designed to get him to hand over money. The team’s access to the scammer is unprecedented, meaning they can see him running his criminal scam, live from his bedroom via his own webcam. And having access to the fraudster’s computer means that Nick and Harleen can learn almost everything about him – giving them the perfect opportunity to confront him.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Choirmaster Gareth Malone is hoping that the New Forest property market hits all the right notes as he enlists the help of Sonali Shah to find him and his family a new home in the Hampshire countryside. With mum Sian along for assistance, Gareth has one big request: to find a property with enough space to fit a grand piano! A beautifully converted former schoolhouse may just provide the answer, but the endless possibilities and potential at a 1920s thatched cottage really strike a chord with the music maestro.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Jan, Mick, Shirl and Dave – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

She also picks out some arty purchases from the show’s archives and counts down the most profitable items at auction. Along the way, Christina Trevanion visits the studio of an art restorer who brings works of art back to their former glory, and Charlie Ross is in mid Wales to meet an artist who sculpts countryside animals from clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team investigate the work of a scammer pretending to be from Amazon. He is trying to scam a man in the UK by saying that hackers have access to his online account, but it’s all a lie designed to get him to hand over money. The team’s access to the scammer is unprecedented, meaning they can see him running his criminal scam, live from his bedroom via his own webcam. And having access to the fraudster’s computer means that Nick and Harleen can learn almost everything about him – giving them the perfect opportunity to confront him.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Choirmaster Gareth Malone is hoping that the New Forest property market hits all the right notes as he enlists the help of Sonali Shah to find him and his family a new home in the Hampshire countryside. With mum Sian along for assistance, Gareth has one big request: to find a property with enough space to fit a grand piano! A beautifully converted former schoolhouse may just provide the answer, but the endless possibilities and potential at a 1920s thatched cottage really strike a chord with the music maestro.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in stunning south west Wales, helping Carol, along with her husband, return to the country where she grew up. With her son Greg supporting her on the house hunt, she’s dreaming of a home close to the sea. The property line-up includes a picture-perfect double-fronted house with roses around the door, and a mystery house boasting spectacular mountain views... it’s Wales at its most wonderful.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Jan, Mick, Shirl and Dave – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: 1993. Niall is conflicted when asked by his mother to lie in court about Ruben’s violence. Ruben seems to have changed for the better, so the decision weighs heavily on him.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring comedian and actor Charlie Brooks, Dr Amir Khan, presenter Sara Damergi and comedian Tim Vine as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.desc: The oversight team face controversy around the tournament’s official new football when a conspiracy theorist claims it has suspect technology inside it. Will accidentally inspires a social media campaign for Sarah’s latest sustainability initiative. But as the ball issue escalates to cause political fallout, it looks as if Sarah’s campaign will be over before it starts. Someone needs to give a statement to the press. And it turns out that someone is Ian.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a thrilling new railway adventure following the Silk Road through the most populous country of Central Asia, Uzbekistan. At the meeting point of east and west, this region has been home to some of the world’s greatest empires: ruled by the Mongols, the ferocious conqueror Tamerlane, imperial Russia and the Soviet Union. Michael begins in the capital, Tashkent, where he takes in its vast, vibrant market and samples popular Uzbek delicacies. He travels on the lavishly decorated Soviet-era metro, which was hidden from the outside world until 2018, when a ban on photographing it was lifted. Michael hears how an earthquake resulted in Tashkent becoming the capital of Soviet modernist architecture, and he makes his TikTok debut with a globally famous Uzbek social media star.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In east Yorkshire, police officer Richard Fussey and local farmer Gordon Calvert discover a suspected gang of nighthawkers – illegal metal detectorists accused of stealing historic treasures under the cover of darkness. When the pair stumble upon men digging on farmland near the ancient Roman road of Woldgate, a tense midnight confrontation unfolds. But when back-up arrives, the question remains: will police find enough evidence to prove the crime and protect Britain’s buried heritage? In Hertfordshire, farmers and police fight back against illegal fly tipping on farmland – a problem reaching epidemic proportions, choking the countryside and leaving landowners to foot the bill. And in County Durham, reporter Paul Colgan investigates the enduring crime of livestock rustling, meeting a farmer whose stolen animals cost him thousands, and officers trialling a bold new operation to stop thieves in their tracks.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists head to the beach to try to find a daughter’s lost bracelet, given to her by her loving foster parents. A 160-year-old find leads archive detective Sam on a fascinating trail, which involves the author of Sherlock Holmes, and crafter Sally is inspired by the history of a Brown Betty teapot fished out of the lake.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores how technology is transforming life for deaf people, from communication tools, English-to-BSL translation and AI to new ways of connecting, working and living in a digital world. Presenter Rolf Choutan is joined in the studio by Billy-Jack Gerrard, who is passionate about AI and how it is shaping the future. He explains how AI works, how coding underpins everyday technology and how his own experiences as a deaf coder have influenced his AI career path and thinking.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie asks the questions as four more contenders take the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the history of the Orkney Islands, the films of Laurel and Hardy, Elizabeth David and Sir Garfield Sobers.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Bristol to help organise a busy and cluttered home. The family, which includes three children under five, is struggling to find space for all their bikes, and the unusual layout of their front room needs some clever thinking to maximise the space and storage.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The team witness a baby boom in the delta. Vianet Djenguet follows lioness Matho as she struggles to raise her cubs alone. Tristen Woodward and Brad Bestelink get a glimpse of Xudum the leopard’s newborn cubs, but dangerous male leopards loom nearby. And with competition growing from the enormous lion pride, Anna Dimitriadis tracks a cheetah mother to the very edge of the territory, where she has been pushed to keep her cubs alive.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel takes the experts across the Atlantic to Ottawa for a special edition set in the National Gallery of Canada. Among the finds are a bronze figure obtained in exchange for a pound of coffee, a desk which started life as a musical instrument, a pair of 19th-century 'whirlygigs', wooden bird scarers, rescued from a chicken coop and worth £10,000 and, the real star of the show, a 16th-century emerald jewelled cross which could be worth £25,000.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: At Blackburn Cathedral, experts Charles Hanson and Anita Manning are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Charles is valuing a rare Eureka clock and Anita is drawn to four oil paintings of the Ribble Valley. Paul Martin meets up with Michelin-star chef Nigel Haworth to discover how to make the perfect Lancashire hotpot.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his railway tour through Uzbekistan on Tashkent’s suburban electric railway to one of the most spectacular and secretive pieces of Soviet Cold War engineering. Hidden high in the mountains, Michael discovers an installation straight out of a Bond movie - a solar furnace that concentrates the sun’s rays into a beam so hot it cuts through steel. From Tashkent, he picks up the high-speed train west to Samarkand and discovers how China’s Belt and Road Initiative is re-establishing old Silk Road routes with new railway connections. Arriving in the legendary ancient city fulfils a lifelong ambition for Michael. He is overwhelmed by the magnificent architecture of the Registan and moved by traditional music played at its heart. Finally, at one of Central Asia’s most important archaeological sites, Afrosiyob, 7th-century Sogdian wall paintings reveal the diverse and cosmopolitan history of this former Silk Road capital.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: If you know where to look, Provence is world class when it comes to excellent, affordable produce. Marcus is taking a deep dive into how the French produce and cook two of his favourite ingredients, beef and tomatoes.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The designers head to Somerset to transform sailors' mess decks at Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. They must turn them into vibrant morale-boosting spaces where the young recruits can cook, eat and socialise. Olympic champion and ex-service woman Dame Kelly Holmes joins Michelle to judge the rooms.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig takes a look at veggies with Jason Manford, Ahir Shah, Holly Walsh and Alan Davies.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: Meticulous and methodical, Big John engineers his ransom scheme with military precision. On paper, it’s flawless. But as the deadline approaches, nothing goes according to plan, and two battles unfold simultaneously: a high-stakes ransom exchange and a desperate race to stop a bomb designed to be unstoppable. Precision planning meets a chaotic reality, and one miscalculation on either side could mean catastrophe.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Growing Up Jewish
programme.desc: Four young people on the cusp of adulthood prepare for one of the biggest nights of their lives – their Bar and Bat Mitzvah – balancing culture, religion and the chance to party.

programme.title: The Theory of Everything
programme.desc: A look at the relationship between the famous physicist Stephen Hawking and his wife.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the Usk valley, from Newport’s urban wildlife to ground-nesting birds, a huge lesser horseshoe bat roost and scarce firecrests.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

Precision planning meets a chaotic reality, and one miscalculation on either side could mean catastrophe.

programme.title: Newsnight

programme.title: Growing Up Jewish
programme.desc: Four young people on the cusp of adulthood prepare for one of the biggest nights of their lives – their Bar and Bat Mitzvah – balancing culture, religion and the chance to party.

programme.title: The Theory of Everything
programme.desc: A look at the relationship between the famous physicist Stephen Hawking and his wife.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the Usk valley, from Newport’s urban wildlife to ground-nesting birds, a huge lesser horseshoe bat roost and scarce firecrests.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: With the leaderboard closer than ever, all four teams leave Zaamin National Park and race towards the next checkpoint, Almaty, Kazakhstan’s former Soviet-era capital.

programme.title: Twenty Twenty Six
programme.desc: The oversight team face controversy around the tournament’s official new football when a conspiracy theorist claims it has suspect technology inside it. Will accidentally inspires a social media campaign for Sarah’s latest sustainability initiative. But as the ball issue escalates to cause political fallout, it looks as if Sarah’s campaign will be over before it starts. Someone needs to give a statement to the press. And it turns out that someone is Ian.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a thrilling new railway adventure following the Silk Road through the most populous country of Central Asia, Uzbekistan. At the meeting point of east and west, this region has been home to some of the world’s greatest empires: ruled by the Mongols, the ferocious conqueror Tamerlane, imperial Russia and the Soviet Union. Michael begins in the capital, Tashkent, where he takes in its vast, vibrant market and samples popular Uzbek delicacies. He travels on the lavishly decorated Soviet-era metro, which was hidden from the outside world until 2018, when a ban on photographing it was lifted. Michael hears how an earthquake resulted in Tashkent becoming the capital of Soviet modernist architecture, and he makes his TikTok debut with a globally famous Uzbek social media star.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In east Yorkshire, police officer Richard Fussey and local farmer Gordon Calvert discover a suspected gang of nighthawkers – illegal metal detectorists accused of stealing historic treasures under the cover of darkness. When the pair stumble upon men digging on farmland near the ancient Roman road of Woldgate, a tense midnight confrontation unfolds. But when back-up arrives, the question remains: will police find enough evidence to prove the crime and protect Britain’s buried heritage? In Hertfordshire, farmers and police fight back against illegal fly tipping on farmland – a problem reaching epidemic proportions, choking the countryside and leaving landowners to foot the bill. And in County Durham, reporter Paul Colgan investigates the enduring crime of livestock rustling, meeting a farmer whose stolen animals cost him thousands, and officers trialling a bold new operation to stop thieves in their tracks.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists head to the beach to try to find a daughter’s lost bracelet, given to her by her loving foster parents. A 160-year-old find leads archive detective Sam on a fascinating trail, which involves the author of Sherlock Holmes, and crafter Sally is inspired by the history of a Brown Betty teapot fished out of the lake.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores how technology is transforming life for deaf people, from communication tools, English-to-BSL translation and AI to new ways of connecting, working and living in a digital world. Presenter Rolf Choutan is joined in the studio by Billy-Jack Gerrard, who is passionate about AI and how it is shaping the future. He explains how AI works, how coding underpins everyday technology and how his own experiences as a deaf coder have influenced his AI career path and thinking.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie asks the questions as four more contenders take the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the history of the Orkney Islands, the films of Laurel and Hardy, Elizabeth David and Sir Garfield Sobers.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Bristol to help organise a busy and cluttered home. The family, which includes three children under five, is struggling to find space for all their bikes, and the unusual layout of their front room needs some clever thinking to maximise the space and storage.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The team witness a baby boom in the delta. Vianet Djenguet follows lioness Matho as she struggles to raise her cubs alone. Tristen Woodward and Brad Bestelink get a glimpse of Xudum the leopard’s newborn cubs, but dangerous male leopards loom nearby. And with competition growing from the enormous lion pride, Anna Dimitriadis tracks a cheetah mother to the very edge of the territory, where she has been pushed to keep her cubs alive.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel takes the experts across the Atlantic to Ottawa for a special edition set in the National Gallery of Canada. Among the finds are a bronze figure obtained in exchange for a pound of coffee, a desk which started life as a musical instrument, a pair of 19th-century 'whirlygigs', wooden bird scarers, rescued from a chicken coop and worth £10,000 and, the real star of the show, a 16th-century emerald jewelled cross which could be worth £25,000.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: At Blackburn Cathedral, experts Charles Hanson and Anita Manning are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Charles is valuing a rare Eureka clock and Anita is drawn to four oil paintings of the Ribble Valley. Paul Martin meets up with Michelin-star chef Nigel Haworth to discover how to make the perfect Lancashire hotpot.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his railway tour through Uzbekistan on Tashkent’s suburban electric railway to one of the most spectacular and secretive pieces of Soviet Cold War engineering. Hidden high in the mountains, Michael discovers an installation straight out of a Bond movie - a solar furnace that concentrates the sun’s rays into a beam so hot it cuts through steel. From Tashkent, he picks up the high-speed train west to Samarkand and discovers how China’s Belt and Road Initiative is re-establishing old Silk Road routes with new railway connections. Arriving in the legendary ancient city fulfils a lifelong ambition for Michael. He is overwhelmed by the magnificent architecture of the Registan and moved by traditional music played at its heart. Finally, at one of Central Asia’s most important archaeological sites, Afrosiyob, 7th-century Sogdian wall paintings reveal the diverse and cosmopolitan history of this former Silk Road capital.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: If you know where to look, Provence is world class when it comes to excellent, affordable produce. Marcus is taking a deep dive into how the French produce and cook two of his favourite ingredients, beef and tomatoes.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The designers head to Somerset to transform sailors' mess decks at Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. They must turn them into vibrant morale-boosting spaces where the young recruits can cook, eat and socialise. Olympic champion and ex-service woman Dame Kelly Holmes joins Michelle to judge the rooms.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig takes a look at veggies with Jason Manford, Ahir Shah, Holly Walsh and Alan Davies.

Hidden high in the mountains, Michael discovers an installation straight out of a Bond movie - a solar furnace that concentrates the sun’s rays into a beam so hot it cuts through steel. From Tashkent, he picks up the high-speed train west to Samarkand and discovers how China’s Belt and Road Initiative is re-establishing old Silk Road routes with new railway connections. Arriving in the legendary ancient city fulfils a lifelong ambition for Michael. He is overwhelmed by the magnificent architecture of the Registan and moved by traditional music played at its heart. Finally, at one of Central Asia’s most important archaeological sites, Afrosiyob, 7th-century Sogdian wall paintings reveal the diverse and cosmopolitan history of this former Silk Road capital.

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: Jack is just 13 years old, but he is already one of the best young darts players in the world. As the British youth darts champion, he has his sights set on an even bigger title: world champion. Jack travels to Gibraltar for the World Junior Open, where he will compete both in the singles and as part of the England squad. However, the road to victory won’t be easy, as Jack has previously lost a world final against Luke Littler, who has since gone on to become professional world champion at just 17. Can Jack turn the tables and bring home the gold? We follow Jack as he trains, competes and faces off against his biggest rivals, including his England teammate Archie, currently ranked number one in the world. With fast-paced action, nail-biting matches and the pressure of playing for his country, we follow the highs and lows of Jack’s road to the top.

programme.desc: Dr Chris and Dr Xand continue to find out more from the team of experts and explorers in Greenland. In this episode, they leave their camp high above Store Glacier and head out across the high Arctic seas in the good ship Neptune. They are in search of the amazing sight that is the Petermann iceberg. At a gigantic two billion tonnes of ice, it is the biggest object afloat in the northern ocean. They attempt the difficult and dangerous task of docking the ship to the berg. The ship's captain Ragi is under pressure, as his target is moving.

programme.title: Art Ninja

programme.title: Deadly Mission Shark
programme.desc: Bad weather causes sea sickness amongst the team, and their next diving lesson has to be abandoned. Steve worries they are running out of time and gives his recruits a pep talk to try and boost spirits. He takes the team to Honeymoon Harbour, an island location where they can meet some magnificent rays. Then it's time for a marathon clean-up as half the team comb the beach for litter. Meanwhile, the others join Steve for an underwater clean-up of the seagrass beds that help make the area a shark sanctuary.

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: What would it look like if a lifetime’s tears fell in one massive drop? That’s what Dr Chris and Dr Xand are determined to find out in Don’t Try This at Home! Gladiator Dynamite is back to put Dr Dan and Dr Raph’s lungs to the test in an unusual Body Battle. In Investigation Ouch, Dr Xand makes a poo donation in the name of medical science, and minds are bent by Dr Chris and Dr Xand, who use pictures by the mysterious street artist Xandsy to trick the eyes and brains of passers-by. At the emergency department in Liverpool, Elinor arrives with a knee injury after falling during a hurdles race at her athletics club, and Naveah has accidentally swallowed a 20 pence piece on a visit to the swimming pool.

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: Jack is just 13 years old, but he is already one of the best young darts players in the world. As the British youth darts champion, he has his sights set on an even bigger title: world champion. Jack travels to Gibraltar for the World Junior Open, where he will compete both in the singles and as part of the England squad. However, the road to victory won’t be easy, as Jack has previously lost a world final against Luke Littler, who has since gone on to become professional world champion at just 17. Can Jack turn the tables and bring home the gold? We follow Jack as he trains, competes and faces off against his biggest rivals, including his England teammate Archie, currently ranked number one in the world. With fast-paced action, nail-biting matches and the pressure of playing for his country, we follow the highs and lows of Jack’s road to the top.
