programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a living room where they watch a lady wrapping up a present. When the lady falls asleep, the Twirlywoos come out and find some other things around the room to wrap. They get carried away and the lady wakes up to find her whole room covered in wrapping paper, including the chair she is sitting in! The Stop-Go Car visits the boat, bringing a long woolly scarf, which the Twirlywoos get wrapped up in. They get so cosy that they fall asleep, and Peekaboo comes out to investigate. He wraps himself up in the scarf and rolls back into his house.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie meets Kian and Monroe at the park, where they gather natural materials together. Mr Tumble gets messy trying to paint a picture. The spotty surprise combines art and nature as everyone makes their own portrait using the natural materials they have found in the park. Featuring signs for the words stick, picture and flower.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: All the Teletubbies are stuck. Tinky Winky's hand is stuck in his bag, Dipsy's hat is stuck, Laa-Laa's ball is stuck and Po is stuck on the Tubby Slidey!

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Addi, Bonnie, Ian, Gracie, Connor, Dhilan and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Gloves which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate gloves inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun nursery rhyme ‘Incy Wincy Spider’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children build block bridges, learn signs for London, bridge and falling down, and sing and sign London Bridge Is Falling Down.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: It’s a busy day down in the garden, as Aaron, Adrian and Nelly are looking for minibeasts! Their journey starts when they lift some logs and stones to see what’s underneath, uncovering a family of woodlice scuttling around. But where are they going, and what’s the rush? Right on cue, Chatterpot’s ready with a clever clue to help Aaron and the buds find the answer.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It’s a really hot day in the attic, and Murphi needs to cool the place down to stop Rebecca getting crabby. A paper plate crab is the first make of the day, with the usual supportive song from the Fabulous Fluffs. An old wooden spoon becomes a spoon monster, thanks to the creativity of the Mini Monsters, and Rebecca’s cousin builds a paper bag house. The Recycling Express provides yogurt pots for a palm tree, and the Tiny Helpers make the leaves.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Minty tries to fly and is mistaken for a Baby Bokchoydacty by its mother.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee thought his tie was a little bit plain, so he added some accessories and now it looks amazing. The Squirrels admire Duggee’s new look and want to learn how to accessorise themselves. The first step for the Squirrels is to find something they’d like to change. The Squirrels each bring a different item - wellies, a T-shirt, headband, helmet and… a potato. They grab sequins, patches, feathers and lights, and then showcase what they have all done. Norrie has added sequins to her T-shirt and made it into a new wonderfully sparkly outfit. Betty has added loads of useful items to her headband, like a calculator and a pencil, to wear it on all occasions. Roly has painted glow-in-the-dark paint on his wellies, and now he can splash in the dark. Tag has painted his helmet and added horns so he looks super-turbo! Roly has turned his potato into a beautifully made-up face with pink and yellow hair. The Squirrels want to accessorise everything. Soon enough, the whole of the Clubhouse and the town are new and improved, but the Squirrels are getting tired. There’s a chance they may have got carried away, so they go to work toning it down a touch. Less is more!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Take a trip with Tino the Artistic Mouse high in the sky or on the ocean. There are hundreds of different ways to travel.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to a place where they’ll make a nature collage using leaves and sticks. On the way, they discover a chocolate river and a bridge that looks like a sheep, choo-choo like an old train and even meet a dragon!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Today, sisters Kyra and Khloe visit a bird centre and meet some friendly owls. With Dad’s help they fly an owl and get it to land on a special protective glove they are holding. Back home, the bird fun continues as the girls make bird masks out of paper plates. But will Mum recognise the two feathered friends flying around the living room?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Kugelis is a recipe from Lithuania that contains bacon and grated potato. Harry has so many potatoes to grate that he has to get his sister to help him! They both work incredibly hard to prepare the dish, which also uses eggs and spring onions. Harry cleverly decorates his table using traditional, beautifully coloured Lithuanian sashes. The kugelis is served with sour cream – let’s hope Harry’s friends love the taste!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie is looking at things we use when we go to the toilet. She visits a factory to see how hand dryers work. She shows us how infrared light is used to switch the machine on and uses her special camera to see water droplets blasted off her hands in slow-motion. Next, Maddie heads to a toilet roll factory to see the how toilet rolls are made. Using a special camera we see inside a pulp-mixing machine, then how a giant mill squeezes the runny mixture into flat sheets of paper that are dried and made into toilet rolls.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika and her family are off to the seaside. Since they’ll be travelling by bus, she and Dr Amit will need to work together to find the way, using the map on Amit’s phone and Kika’s super sight. Once she learns a new route, she stores it in her memory bank. She knows 300 routes already - Kika is like a doggy GPS! Using her waymarks, including a magic picture that turns people into lobsters, a talkative bucket and spade and a giant pile of stinky seaweed, Kika successfully guides her family to the beach. But when they stop for some delicious fish and chips on the way back, Amit and Seema realise Anoushka has left her jacket on the beach. Kika calls on her super sight to retrace her steps with Amit. But will she find their way again? And can she and Amit get back to the bus stop to meet their family before the bus leaves for home? The race is on.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some pygmy marmosets. These tiny monkeys are the smallest in the world - they are about the size of a tennis ball. These treetop athletes can turn their heads nearly halfway around and look backwards. Aneeshwar and Lizzie give it a go. Next, they meet a giant spider with a giant web - the orb weaver spider. When her keeper throws some food onto her web, she immediately feels the vibrations and races to catch it. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection between these two incredible animals is.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's Waffle's birthday and Mr Willow throws a huge party for him. As the Brooklyn-Bells prepare a surprise for Waffle, Connie and Ruby's dog, Jelly, leads the Wonder Dog astray.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Dragonflies are amazing! Oona and her friends want to watch them fly.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Yukee’s precious clockwork music box breaks, her garden friends cheer her up with a life-size clockwork performance of their own.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: While looking for a spoon for her yogurt, Maddie realises that all the teaspoons have gone missing - it's like they all got up and marched off! Maddie is on hand to find a surprisingly musical way to get them back where they belong.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels become architects so they can design, build and bring to life their very own clubhouse.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Three arrives with a bang and a song-and-dance about her favourite number - 1, 2, 3, Everybody Look at Me! Learn all about the number three with Numberblock Three.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: Alphablock G and her friends come across Alphablock S pushing up some mysterious signs. They learn to read them and discover that each one is an instruction. JOG tells them to run on a travelator. They HOP across some stepping stones and then clamber UP a net. Finally, they GET IN a gravity ball that rolls them back to the start of what they now realise is a super game devised by S. They can’t wait to have another go.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: It’s a hot day, so Justin and his friends cool off by visiting an ice cream farm. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble tries to keep Spotty cool but can’t seem to control his hosepipe!

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po take it in turns to listen to music through a pair of headphones. The Teletubbies love dancing to the music they hear.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how orchards play an important role in the environment. They find out that orchards are mosaic habitats which attract lots of different plants and wildlife and provide shelter and protection for so many creatures. On the way, they spot some fallen fruit that is great for animals to eat and try some fruit that grows in an orchard which they can enjoy too!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: When a rogue ball destroys Mr Parks’s competition-ready bug hotel, Evie, Taran and Jaz help him rebuild it using a combination of football skills and teamwork.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that only have three wheels! Grace drives a really fast off-road buggy, shows off incredible off-road trucks and then rides a quad bike.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Dodge has the final say on whether the class have Golden Hour inside or outside. Half the class want to play inside, whilst the rest of the class want to play outside. Dodge struggles with the decision but eventually makes up his mind - only for it all to change again.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie pretend to be pirates and head to a nearby boating lake. But will they find any treasure?

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: A honey badger claims a watering hole, so Kwazii challenges her to a digging contest.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: A simple matter of duckling-sitting turns into a potential disaster when the ducklings escape into the wood.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie skips into the Clubhouse and greets her friends. Together, they reflect on their first meeting. Arriving with her parents in a long limousine, Norrie, her parents and her 72 siblings flood out of the car. It's just Norrie who is going to stay at the Clubhouse, though, and enjoy some well-needed quiet. She can play alone and hear herself think! But after a while, she misses the hustle and bustle, so Duggee introduces Norrie to Enid the cat. Together, they venture into the Clubhouse, and Norrie has a friend so she isn't alone, but she still has a little bit more room than she would have at home!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny gets a tummy ache from not washing his hands, so Vida teaches him all about germs - and helps his tummy!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea steals Tomato’s precious jewel. Supertato ventures to get it back by secretly lifting the jewel from Evil Pea’s crown and defeating a crowd of rampaging Mini Peas.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings lose a relay race against the eaglets and are fed up with Weasy for not cheering them on. As Papa Eagle comes to show off, Weasy decides to challenge this pretentious family. It's time to train, but Weasy becomes an unbearable coach.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Tao needs help learning to fly his new wingsuit for a big town event, and Mojo and Bo are the experts. Can they help him find his inner bird before it’s too late?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The kids are delivering mud pizzas to the grown-ups, but their pedal car keeps breaking.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Flutter accidentally clones himself, leaving the berg flooded with scores of badly behaved penguins. As trouble spreads, the Piris must find a way to lose the unruly duplicates.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Penny brings a dinosaur fossil to the nursery, while Bonnie and Hamish plan a secret dino dance. And mysterious footprints have Penny wondering if there’s a real dino on the island.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle learns that the summer holidays will soon be over and Evie will be going to school. Determined not to be left alone, Waffle hatches a plan to keep the family at home.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi longs for adventure, but Deborah prefers to rest. With a swish of her wishing wand, Tornado appears - a confident, glittering unicorn, bursting with heroic energy. Together, they gallop through the Bake A Wish café, turning cake deliveries into daring quests and baby food spills into perilous lakes. As the adventure shows no sign of stopping, Rafi realises it’s okay to rest. Luckily, her dads and sleepy Deborah remind her that sometimes the cosiest adventures are found at home.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: When Gran Gran and JoJo find a family recipe for Great Gran Gran’s signature Saint Lucian banana bread, they’re excited to bake a batch of it! But there’s one problem - cake mix has been spilt on the recipe, so they don’t know how long to bake it for!

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah finds an umbrella that doesn't seem to like the rain.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small comes to the rescue when Granny, Major, Mother and the Soup Dragon get into trouble.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa have fun spotting the Yummies, who are popping up all over BeddyByes. At Play Time, the Yummies pop up and disappear again whilst MeMo and BaBa play with a beepy horn. They take it to Yummy Land, where the Yummies explain that they are looking everywhere for Yummy Dog. MeMo and BaBa help to look, beeping the horn as they go. Yummy Dog hears the horn and is reunited with the Yummies.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Pontipines are eating their dinner when Mr Pontipine's moustache flies off. First it gets stuck on the chimney, then the bridge and then the gazebo. Mr Pontipine's moustache ends up stuck to the Pinky Ponk's propeller. It blows the moustache back towards the Pontipines. Everybody joins in the dance at the gazebo.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Olivia Colman tells the classic tale of the Gruffalo's Child in a Bedtime Story.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Gooseberry singing a song about everything you have to do to become a Gooseberry Club member.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Pando discover a new climbing frame at the playground. It has climbing bits, tippy bits and even a wobbly bridge. But when Bing gets to the top of the slide, it's too scary for him to go down. Bing watches Pando to see how he does it, then he helps Hoppity Voosh to go down. When Hoppity likes it, Bing has a go too.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies say 'eh-oh' to each other in turn and then say 'eh-oh' to flowers, while the children in Tummy Tales make a friendship circle out of handprints.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Preschool animation about a baby monkey and his mother. When Mo wakes up with a cold, Tee takes over mum duties.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: The veggies are playing walkie-talkie hide-and-seek, but Evil Pea steals Carrot’s walkie-talkie and uses it to trick the Veggies into getting trapped by the Corn Cobs.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Nicky are sleeping over at Sula's house, but Bing has forgotten Hoppity! The wind causes a branch to make a scratchy noise that terrifies Bing, who isn't very comforted by Sula's fairy rhino. Amma phones Flop, while Sula, Nicky and Bing play 'Nicky tickles' as they wait. Flop arrives, bringing his sleeping bag and Hoppity so they can all sleep over.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: A camping trip with Preston goes very wrong when he won’t let them use Mojo’s tops. But camping Preston’s way soon starts a fire. It’s Mojo and Bo to the rescue!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Watch the Penguins play ping-pong, laugh along with John the Crab on his chat show, and help Jet Rocket discover his talents.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have just got some new walkie-talkies and are having so much fun with them. Duggee calls the Squirrels to come for some blueberry juice, but as Tag is running, he trips over a car and falls through a secret door in the wall! Communicating through his walkie-talkie, Tag doesn’t know where he is. He can see lots and lots of things around him but no one has any idea where this room is in the house!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The kids are delivering mud pizzas to the grown-ups, but their pedal car keeps breaking.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch makes the Statue of Liberty fall right into the path of a passing ferry. Go Jetters, Go!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. The Octopod is attacked by a colossal squid, who drags the ship down an abyssal trench, forcing Barnacles and Kwazii to make a perilous swim outside to confront the gigantic beast.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Are you sitting comfortably? Then we'll begin a bedtime story all about Numberblocks Six to Ten. Learn all about the numbers 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: TH, I and NG make something spectacular - but what is it? It's marvellous, mechanical and musical and everyone wants one! This episode introduces the 'th-' digraph and the words thing, this, that, thick, thin and them.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: It’s a rainy day, and Nick and Norman are bored. What can they do? The Popcast Planners help write a rainy day song and have lots of fun ideas for Nick and Norman to do outside.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella pretends to be a cat. With ears, paws and a miaow... it’s Bella-Cat! Together with Lift, she explores the floors of Playtime Towers. In the Ice Disco, Hettie has an idea for a cat dance with the Playtimers. In the Cloud Kitchen, Patch recalls a time he had breakfast with some cats called the Fusspot Tigers, who just love to munch marvellous marmalade! Meanwhile, in the Sing Song Forest, Tincy the Spider finds lots of cuddly animals in her web, and she knows a special spider rhyme all about taily-waily animals!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing takes his Hoppity Voosh toy to the park to see the ducks and play on the slide. But when he steps in dog poo and heads to Amma's house to get cleaned up, he leaves Hoppity behind. Amma helps Bing to focus so that he can remember where he went and retrace his steps to find Hoppity.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘ant’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of ants – a black one, another with two feelers and a teeny-weeny tiny ant! There are marching ants, a strong one, and Dee meets a queen ant! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu takes the class pet home for the weekend.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou are going to have a feast of their favourite fruit: yum yum baronies. But Lou loses control and eats them all before Kiri can have any!

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: On a rainy day, the Froglets create a shadow show for Bertie and their puppet friends.

JOG tells them to run on a travelator. They HOP across some stepping stones and then clamber UP a net. Finally, they GET IN a gravity ball that rolls them back to the start of what they now realise is a super game devised by S. They can’t wait to have another go.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: It’s a hot day, so Justin and his friends cool off by visiting an ice cream farm. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble tries to keep Spotty cool but can’t seem to control his hosepipe!

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po take it in turns to listen to music through a pair of headphones. The Teletubbies love dancing to the music they hear.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how orchards play an important role in the environment. They find out that orchards are mosaic habitats which attract lots of different plants and wildlife and provide shelter and protection for so many creatures. On the way, they spot some fallen fruit that is great for animals to eat and try some fruit that grows in an orchard which they can enjoy too!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: When a rogue ball destroys Mr Parks’s competition-ready bug hotel, Evie, Taran and Jaz help him rebuild it using a combination of football skills and teamwork.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that only have three wheels! Grace drives a really fast off-road buggy, shows off incredible off-road trucks and then rides a quad bike.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Dodge has the final say on whether the class have Golden Hour inside or outside. Half the class want to play inside, whilst the rest of the class want to play outside. Dodge struggles with the decision but eventually makes up his mind - only for it all to change again.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie pretend to be pirates and head to a nearby boating lake. But will they find any treasure?

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: A honey badger claims a watering hole, so Kwazii challenges her to a digging contest.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: A simple matter of duckling-sitting turns into a potential disaster when the ducklings escape into the wood.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie skips into the Clubhouse and greets her friends. Together, they reflect on their first meeting. Arriving with her parents in a long limousine, Norrie, her parents and her 72 siblings flood out of the car. It's just Norrie who is going to stay at the Clubhouse, though, and enjoy some well-needed quiet. She can play alone and hear herself think! But after a while, she misses the hustle and bustle, so Duggee introduces Norrie to Enid the cat. Together, they venture into the Clubhouse, and Norrie has a friend so she isn't alone, but she still has a little bit more room than she would have at home!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny gets a tummy ache from not washing his hands, so Vida teaches him all about germs - and helps his tummy!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea steals Tomato’s precious jewel. Supertato ventures to get it back by secretly lifting the jewel from Evil Pea’s crown and defeating a crowd of rampaging Mini Peas.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings lose a relay race against the eaglets and are fed up with Weasy for not cheering them on. As Papa Eagle comes to show off, Weasy decides to challenge this pretentious family. It's time to train, but Weasy becomes an unbearable coach.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Tao needs help learning to fly his new wingsuit for a big town event, and Mojo and Bo are the experts. Can they help him find his inner bird before it’s too late?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The kids are delivering mud pizzas to the grown-ups, but their pedal car keeps breaking.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Flutter accidentally clones himself, leaving the berg flooded with scores of badly behaved penguins. As trouble spreads, the Piris must find a way to lose the unruly duplicates.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Penny brings a dinosaur fossil to the nursery, while Bonnie and Hamish plan a secret dino dance. And mysterious footprints have Penny wondering if there’s a real dino on the island.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle learns that the summer holidays will soon be over and Evie will be going to school. Determined not to be left alone, Waffle hatches a plan to keep the family at home.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi longs for adventure, but Deborah prefers to rest. With a swish of her wishing wand, Tornado appears - a confident, glittering unicorn, bursting with heroic energy. Together, they gallop through the Bake A Wish café, turning cake deliveries into daring quests and baby food spills into perilous lakes. As the adventure shows no sign of stopping, Rafi realises it’s okay to rest. Luckily, her dads and sleepy Deborah remind her that sometimes the cosiest adventures are found at home.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: When Gran Gran and JoJo find a family recipe for Great Gran Gran’s signature Saint Lucian banana bread, they’re excited to bake a batch of it! But there’s one problem - cake mix has been spilt on the recipe, so they don’t know how long to bake it for!

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah finds an umbrella that doesn't seem to like the rain.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small comes to the rescue when Granny, Major, Mother and the Soup Dragon get into trouble.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa have fun spotting the Yummies, who are popping up all over BeddyByes. At Play Time, the Yummies pop up and disappear again whilst MeMo and BaBa play with a beepy horn. They take it to Yummy Land, where the Yummies explain that they are looking everywhere for Yummy Dog. MeMo and BaBa help to look, beeping the horn as they go. Yummy Dog hears the horn and is reunited with the Yummies.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Pontipines are eating their dinner when Mr Pontipine's moustache flies off. First it gets stuck on the chimney, then the bridge and then the gazebo. Mr Pontipine's moustache ends up stuck to the Pinky Ponk's propeller. It blows the moustache back towards the Pontipines. Everybody joins in the dance at the gazebo.

programme.desc: Olivia Colman tells the classic tale of the Gruffalo's Child in a Bedtime Story.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Lenny Henry faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Who does he regret idolising? In what order does he wash his body parts? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Lenny Henry faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Who does he regret idolising? In what order does he wash his body parts? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.

From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Lenny Henry faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Who does he regret idolising? In what order does he wash his body parts? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Lenny Henry faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Who does he regret idolising? In what order does he wash his body parts? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Lenny Henry faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Who does he regret idolising? In what order does he wash his body parts? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Lenny Henry faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Who does he regret idolising? In what order does he wash his body parts? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Henry reflects on growing up in Britain during a time of overt racism, the impact of Comic Relief, and the difficult choices he's had to forgive himself for. He opens up about family, identity and the discovery that his uncle was his biological father, as well as the loss of his mother and the grief that followed. Along the way, he's asked questions about relationships, legacy and moments that have defined who he is - with time for dancing, a little flirtation and plenty of laughter. From deeply personal revelations to completely unexpected tangents, this is Lenny Henry as you've never seen him before - disarmed, reflective and up for anything - with honesty, warmth and moments that land when you least expect them.
